newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan vehicle output marks biggest gain since 1980.
newsitem.headline: Japan vehicle output marks biggest gain since 1980.

text.p: Strong domestic demand ahead of a sales-tax increase and higher exports due to a weaker yen pushed Japan's monthly vehicle production last month to its biggest gain since 1980, a trade group said Monday.
Domestic production rose more than 19 percent to 917,798 vehicles compared with January 1996, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association said.
It was the fifth successive month of year-on-year gains and the biggest since a nearly 24 percent gain in September 1980, an association official said.

The association said it expects exports in January to show a sharp 34 percent rise from a year earlier and added that this was likely to provoke complaints from the U.S. car industry about the growth in exports.
"The American car industry may complain about higher January exports but the higher exports were mainly because Japan had lower exports in January last year," an association official said.

The association said the output increase was a result of strong domestic demand this year ahead of a scheduled increase in Japan's consumption tax from 3 percent to 5 percent on April 1 and higher exports due to the weaker yen.
The yen traded at about 106 yen to the dollar in January 1996 compared with about 123 yen at the end of this January.
The association said production rose at all 11 Japanese vehicle makers in January and domestic sales, including those of 660 cc mini vehicles, rose 11.5 percent from a year earlier to 446,192.
